sanskrit_shloka:
इत्थं विपश्चित्सदसद्विभज्य निश्चित्य तत्त्वं निजबोधदृष्ट्या ।
ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमखण्डबोधं तेभ्यो विमुक्तः स्वयमेव शाम्यति ॥ ३५२ ॥
transliteration:
itthaṃ vipaścitsadasadvibhajya niścitya tattvaṃ nijabodhadṛṣṭyā |
jñātvā svamātmānamakhaṇḍabodhaṃ tebhyo vimuktaḥ svayameva śāmyati || 352 ||
translation: The wise man, discriminating thus the real and the unreal, ascertaining the Truth through his illuminative insight, and realising his own Self which is Knowledge Absolute, gets rid of the obstructions and directly attains Peace.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The wise man, discriminating thus the real and the unreal, ascertaining the Truth through his illuminative insight, and realising his own Self which is Knowledge Absolute, gets rid of the obstructions and directly attains Peace.

sanskrit_shloka:
अज्ञानहृदयग्रन्थेर्निःशेषविलयस्तदा ।
समाधिनाविकल्पेन यदाद्वैतात्मदर्शनम् ॥ ३५३ ॥
transliteration:
ajñānahṛdayagrantherniḥśeṣavilayastadā |
samādhināvikalpena yadādvaitātmadarśanam || 353 ||
translation: When the Ātman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the Ātman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

sanskrit_shloka:
अज्ञानहृदयग्रन्थेर्निःशेषविलयस्तदा ।
समाधिनाविकल्पेन यदाद्वैतात्मदर्शनम् ॥ ३५३ ॥
transliteration:
ajñānahṛdayagrantherniḥśeṣavilayastadā |
samādhināvikalpena yadādvaitātmadarśanam || 353 ||
translation: When the Ātman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the Ātman, the One without a second, is realised by means of the Nirvikalpa Samadhi, then the heart’s knot of ignorance is totally destroyed.

sanskrit_shloka:
त्वमहमिदमितीयं कल्पना बुद्धिदोषात् प्रभवति परमात्मन्यद्वये निर्विशेषे ।
प्रविलसति समाधावस्य सर्वो विकल्पो विलयनमुपगच्छेद्वस्तुतत्त्वावधृत्या ॥ ३५४ ॥
transliteration:
tvamahamidamitīyaṃ kalpanā buddhidoṣāt prabhavati paramātmanyadvaye nirviśeṣe |
pravilasati samādhāvasya sarvo vikalpo vilayanamupagacchedvastutattvāvadhṛtyā || 354 ||
translation: Such imaginations as 'thou', 'I' or 'this' take place through the defects of the Buddhi. But when the Paramātman, the Absolute, the One without a second, manifests Itself in Samadhi, all such imaginations are dissolved for the aspirant, through the realisation of the truth of Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Such imaginations as 'thou', 'I' or 'this' take place through the defects of the Buddhi. But when the Paramātman, the Absolute, the One without a second, manifests Itself in Samadhi, all such imaginations are dissolved for the aspirant, through the realisation of the truth of Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
शान्तो दान्तः परमुपरतः क्षान्तियुक्तः समाधिं कुर्वन्नित्यं कलयति यतिः स्वस्य सर्वात्मभावम् ।
तेनाविद्यातिमिरजनितान्साधु दग्ध्वा विकल्पान् ब्रह्माकृत्या निवसति सुखं निष्क्रियो निर्विकल्पः ॥ ३५५ ॥
transliteration:
śānto dāntaḥ paramuparataḥ kṣāntiyuktaḥ samādhiṃ kurvannityaṃ kalayati yatiḥ svasya sarvātmabhāvam |
tenāvidyātimirajanitānsādhu dagdhvā vikalpān brahmākṛtyā nivasati sukhaṃ niṣkriyo nirvikalpaḥ || 355 ||
translation: The Sannyasin, calm, self-controlled, perfectly retiring from the sense-world, forbearing, and devoting himself to the practice of Samadhi, always reflects on his own self being the Self of the whole universe. Destroying completely by this means the imaginations which are due to the gloom of ignorance, he lives blissfully as Brahman, free from action and the oscillations of the mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Sannyasin, calm, self-controlled, perfectly retiring from the sense-world, forbearing, and devoting himself to the practice of Samadhi, always reflects on his own self being the Self of the whole universe. Destroying completely by this means the imaginations which are due to the gloom of ignorance, he lives blissfully as Brahman, free from action and the oscillations of the mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
समाहिता ये प्रविलाप्य बाह्यं श्रोत्रादि चेतः स्वमहं चिदात्मनि ।
त एव मुक्ता भवपाशबन्धैः नान्ये तु पारोक्ष्यकथाभिधायिनः ॥ ३५६ ॥
transliteration:
samāhitā ye pravilāpya bāhyaṃ śrotrādi cetaḥ svamahaṃ cidātmani |
ta eva muktā bhavapāśabandhaiḥ nānye tu pārokṣyakathābhidhāyinaḥ || 356 ||
translation: Those alone are free from the bondage of transmigration who, attaining Samadhi, have merged the objective world, the sense-organs, the mind, nay, the very ego, in the Ātman, the Knowledge Absolute – and none else, who but dabble in second-hand talks.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Those alone are free from the bondage of transmigration who, attaining Samadhi, have merged the objective world, the sense-organs, the mind, nay, the very ego, in the Ātman, the Knowledge Absolute – and none else, who but dabble in second-hand talks.

sanskrit_shloka:
उपाधिभेदात्स्वयमेव भिद्यते चोपाध्यपोहे स्वयमेव केवलः ।
तस्मादुपाधेर्विलयाय विद्वान् वसेत्सदाकल्पसमाधिनिष्ठया ॥ ३५७ ॥
transliteration:
upādhibhedātsvayameva bhidyate copādhyapohe svayameva kevalaḥ |
tasmādupādhervilayāya vidvān vasetsadākalpasamādhiniṣṭhayā || 357 ||
translation: Through the diversity of the supervening conditions (Upadhis), a man is apt to think of himself as also full of diversity; but with the removal of these he is again his own Self, the immutable. Therefore the wise man should ever devote himself to the practice of Nirvikalpa Samadhi, for the dissolution of the Upadhis.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the diversity of the supervening conditions (Upadhis), a man is apt to think of himself as also full of diversity; but with the removal of these he is again his own Self, the immutable. Therefore the wise man should ever devote himself to the practice of Nirvikalpa Samadhi, for the dissolution of the Upadhis.

sanskrit_shloka:
सति सक्तो नरो याति सद्भावं ह्येकनिष्ठया ।
कीटको भ्रमरं ध्यायन् भ्रमरत्वाय कल्पते ॥ ३५८ ॥
transliteration:
sati sakto naro yāti sadbhāvaṃ hyekaniṣṭhayā |
kīṭako bhramaraṃ dhyāyan bhramaratvāya kalpate || 358 ||
translation: The man who is attached to the Real becomes Real, through his one-pointed devotion. Just as the cockroach thinking intently on the Bhramara is transformed into a Bhramara.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The man who is attached to the Real becomes Real, through his one-pointed devotion. Just as the cockroach thinking intently on the Bhramara is transformed into a Bhramara.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्रियान्तरासक्तिमपास्य कीटको ध्यायन्नलित्वं ह्यलिभावमृच्छति ।
तथैव योगी परमात्मतत्त्वं ध्यात्वा समायाति तदेकनिष्ठया ॥ ३५९ ॥
transliteration:
kriyāntarāsaktimapāsya kīṭako dhyāyannalitvaṃ hyalibhāvamṛcchati |
tathaiva yogī paramātmatattvaṃ dhyātvā samāyāti tadekaniṣṭhayā || 359 ||
translation: Just as the cockroach, giving up the attachment to all other actions, thinks intently on the Bhramara and becomes transformed into that worm, exactly in the same manner the Yogi, meditating on the truth of the Paramātman, attains to It through his one- pointed devotion to that.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as the cockroach, giving up the attachment to all other actions, thinks intently on the Bhramara and becomes transformed into that worm, exactly in the same manner the Yogi, meditating on the truth of the Paramātman, attains to It through his one- pointed devotion to that.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतीव सूक्ष्मं परमात्मतत्त्वं न स्थूलदृष्ट्या प्रतिपत्तुमर्हति ।
समाधिनात्यन्तसुसूक्ष्मवृत्या ज्ञातव्यमार्यैरतिशुद्धबुद्धिभिः ॥ ३६0 ॥
transliteration:
atīva sūkṣmaṃ paramātmatattvaṃ na sthūladṛṣṭyā pratipattumarhati |
samādhinātyantasusūkṣmavṛtyā jñātavyamāryairatiśuddhabuddhibhiḥ || 360 ||
translation: The truth of the Paramātman is extremely subtle, and cannot be reached by the gross outgoing tendency of the mind. It is only accessible to noble souls with perfectly pure minds, by means of Samadhi brought on by an extraordinary fineness of the mental state.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The truth of the Paramātman is extremely subtle, and cannot be reached by the gross outgoing tendency of the mind. It is only accessible to noble souls with perfectly pure minds, by means of Samadhi brought on by an extraordinary fineness of the mental state.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा सुवर्णं पुटपाकशोधितं त्यक्त्वा मलं स्वात्मगुणं समृच्छति ।
तथा मनः सत्त्वरजस्तमोमलं ध्यानेन सन्त्यज्य समेति तत्त्वम् ॥ ३६१ ॥
transliteration:
yathā suvarṇaṃ puṭapākaśodhitaṃ tyaktvā malaṃ svātmaguṇaṃ samṛcchati |
tathā manaḥ sattvarajastamomalaṃ dhyānena santyajya sameti tattvam || 361 ||
translation: As gold purified by thorough heating on the fire gives up its impurities and attains to its own lustre, so the mind, through meditation, gives up its impurities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, and attains to the reality of Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As gold purified by thorough heating on the fire gives up its impurities and attains to its own lustre, so the mind, through meditation, gives up its impurities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, and attains to the reality of Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
निरन्तराभ्यासवशात्तदित्थं पक्वं मनो ब्रह्मणि लीयते यदा ।
तदा समाधिः सविकल्पवर्जितः स्वतोऽद्वयानन्दरसानुभावकः ॥ ३६२ ॥
transliteration:
nirantarābhyāsavaśāttaditthaṃ pakvaṃ mano brahmaṇi līyate yadā |
tadā samādhiḥ savikalpavarjitaḥ svato'dvayānandarasānubhāvakaḥ || 362 ||
translation: When the mind, thus purified by constant practice, is merged in Brahman, then Samadhi passes on from the Savikalpa to the Nirvikalpa stage, and leads directly to the realisation of the Bliss of Brahman, the One without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the mind, thus purified by constant practice, is merged in Brahman, then Samadhi passes on from the Savikalpa to the Nirvikalpa stage, and leads directly to the realisation of the Bliss of Brahman, the One without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
समाधिनानेन समस्तवासना ग्रन्थेर्विनाशोऽखिलकर्मनाशः ।
अन्तर्बहिः सर्वत एव सर्वदा स्वरूपविस्फूर्तिरयत्नतः स्यात् ॥ ३६३ ॥
transliteration:
samādhinānena samastavāsanā granthervināśo'khilakarmanāśaḥ |
antarbahiḥ sarvata eva sarvadā svarūpavisphūrtirayatnataḥ syāt || 363 ||
translation: By this Samadhi are destroyed all desires which are like knots, all work is at an end, and inside and out there takes place everywhere and always the spontaneous manifestation of one’s real nature.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: By this Samadhi are destroyed all desires which are like knots, all work is at an end, and inside and out there takes place everywhere and always the spontaneous manifestation of one’s real nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
श्रुतेः शतगुणं विद्यान्मननं मननादपि ।
निदिंध्यासं लक्षगुणमनन्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ॥ ३६४ ॥
transliteration:
śruteḥ śataguṇaṃ vidyānmananaṃ mananādapi |
nidiṃdhyāsaṃ lakṣaguṇamanantaṃ nirvikalpakam || 364 ||
translation: Reflection should be considered a hundred times superior to hearing, and meditation a hundred thousand times superior even to reflection, but the Nirvikalpa Samadhi is infinite in its results.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Reflection should be considered a hundred times superior to hearing, and meditation a hundred thousand times superior even to reflection, but the Nirvikalpa Samadhi is infinite in its results.

sanskrit_shloka:
निर्विकल्पकसमाधिना स्फुटं ब्रह्मतत्त्वमवगम्यते ध्रुवम् ।
नान्यथा चलतया मनोगतेः प्रत्ययान्तरविमिश्रितं भवेत् ॥ ३६५ ॥
transliteration:
nirvikalpakasamādhinā sphuṭaṃ brahmatattvamavagamyate dhruvam |
nānyathā calatayā manogateḥ pratyayāntaravimiśritaṃ bhavet || 365 ||
translation: By the Nirvikalpa Samadhi the truth of Brahman is clearly and definitely realised, but not otherwise, for then the mind, being unstable by nature, is apt to be mixed up with other perceptions.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: By the Nirvikalpa Samadhi the truth of Brahman is clearly and definitely realised, but not otherwise, for then the mind, being unstable by nature, is apt to be mixed up with other perceptions.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतः समाधत्स्व यतेन्द्रियः सन् निरन्तरं शान्तमनाः प्रतीचि ।
विध्वंसय ध्वान्तमनाद्यविद्यया कृतं सदेकत्वविलोकनेन ॥ ३६६ ॥
transliteration:
ataḥ samādhatsva yatendriyaḥ san nirantaraṃ śāntamanāḥ pratīci |
vidhvaṃsaya dhvāntamanādyavidyayā kṛtaṃ sadekatvavilokanena || 366 ||
translation: Hence with the mind calm and the senses controlled always drown the mind in the Supreme Self that is within, and through the realisation of thy identity with that Reality destroy the darkness created by Nescience, which is without beginning.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Hence with the mind calm and the senses controlled always drown the mind in the Supreme Self that is within, and through the realisation of thy identity with that Reality destroy the darkness created by Nescience, which is without beginning.

sanskrit_shloka:
योगस्य प्रथमद्वारं वाङ्निरोधोऽपरिग्रहः ।
निराशा च निरीहा च नित्यमेकान्तशीलता ॥ ३६७ ॥
transliteration:
yogasya prathamadvāraṃ vāṅnirodho'parigrahaḥ |
nirāśā ca nirīhā ca nityamekāntaśīlatā || 367 ||
translation: The first steps to Yoga are control of speech, non-receiving of gifts, entertaining of no expectations, freedom from activity, and always living in a retired place.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The first steps to Yoga are control of speech, non-receiving of gifts, entertaining of no expectations, freedom from activity, and always living in a retired place.

sanskrit_shloka:
एकान्तस्थितिरिन्द्रियोपरमणे हेनुर्दमश्चेतसः संरोधे करणं शमेन विलयं यायादहंवासना ।
तेनानन्दरसानुभूतिरचला ब्राह्मी सदा योगिनः तस्माच्चित्तनिरोध एव सततं कार्यः प्रयत्नो मुनेः ॥ ३६८ ॥
transliteration:
ekāntasthitirindriyoparamaṇe henurdamaścetasaḥ saṃrodhe karaṇaṃ śamena vilayaṃ yāyādahaṃvāsanā |
tenānandarasānubhūtiracalā brāhmī sadā yoginaḥ tasmāccittanirodha eva satataṃ kāryaḥ prayatno muneḥ || 368 ||
translation: Living in a retired place serves to control the sense-organs, control of the senses helps to control the mind, through control of the mind egoism is destroyed; and this again gives the Yogi an unbroken realisation of the Bliss of Brahman. Therefore the man of reflection should always strive only to control the mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Living in a retired place serves to control the sense-organs, control of the senses helps to control the mind, through control of the mind egoism is destroyed; and this again gives the Yogi an unbroken realisation of the Bliss of Brahman. Therefore the man of reflection should always strive only to control the mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
वाचं नियच्छात्मनि तं नियच्छ बुद्धौ धियं यच्छ च बुद्धिसाक्षिणि ।
तं चापि पूर्णात्मनि निर्विकल्पे विलाप्य शान्तिं परमां भजस्व ॥ ३६९ ॥
transliteration:
vācaṃ niyacchātmani taṃ niyaccha buddhau dhiyaṃ yaccha ca buddhisākṣiṇi |
taṃ cāpi pūrṇātmani nirvikalpe vilāpya śāntiṃ paramāṃ bhajasva || 369 ||
translation: Restrain speech in the Manas, and restrain Manas in the Buddhi; this again restrain in the witness of Buddhi, and merging that also in the Infinite Absolute Self, attain to supreme Peace.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Restrain speech in the Manas, and restrain Manas in the Buddhi; this again restrain in the witness of Buddhi, and merging that also in the Infinite Absolute Self, attain to supreme Peace.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहप्राणेन्द्रियमनोबुद्ध्यादिभिरुपाधिभिः ।
यैर्यैर्वृत्तेःसमायोगस्ततद्भावोऽस्य योगिनः ॥ ३७0 ॥
transliteration:
dehaprāṇendriyamanobuddhyādibhirupādhibhiḥ |
yairyairvṛtteḥsamāyogastatadbhāvo'sya yoginaḥ || 370 ||
translation: The body, Prāṇas, organs, manas, Buddhi and the rest – with whichever of these supervening adjuncts the mind is associated, the Yogi is transformed, as it were, into that.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The body, Prāṇas, organs, manas, Buddhi and the rest – with whichever of these supervening adjuncts the mind is associated, the Yogi is transformed, as it were, into that.

sanskrit_shloka:
तन्निवृत्त्या मुनेः सम्यक्सर्वोपरमणं सुखम् ।
संदृश्यते सदानन्दरसानुभवविप्लवः ॥ ३७१ ॥
transliteration:
tannivṛttyā muneḥ samyaksarvoparamaṇaṃ sukham |
saṃdṛśyate sadānandarasānubhavaviplavaḥ || 371 ||
translation: When this is stopped, the man of reflection is found to be easily detached from everything, and to get the experience of an abundance of everlasting Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When this is stopped, the man of reflection is found to be easily detached from everything, and to get the experience of an abundance of everlasting Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
अन्तस्त्यागो बहिस्त्यागो विरक्तस्यैव युज्यते ।
त्यजत्यन्तर्बहिःसङ्गं विरक्तस्तु मुमुक्षया ॥ ३७२ ॥
transliteration:
antastyāgo bahistyāgo viraktasyaiva yujyate |
tyajatyantarbahiḥsaṅgaṃ viraktastu mumukṣayā || 372 ||
translation: It is the man of dispassion (Vairāgya) who is fit for this internal as well as external renunciation; for the dispassionate man, out of the desire to be free, relinquishes both internal and external attachment.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It is the man of dispassion (Vairāgya) who is fit for this internal as well as external renunciation; for the dispassionate man, out of the desire to be free, relinquishes both internal and external attachment.

sanskrit_shloka:
बहिस्तु विषयैः सङ्गं तथान्तरहमादिभिः ।
विरक्त एव शक्नोति त्यक्तुं ब्रह्मणि निष्ठितः ॥ ३७३ ॥
transliteration:
bahistu viṣayaiḥ saṅgaṃ tathāntarahamādibhiḥ |
virakta eva śaknoti tyaktuṃ brahmaṇi niṣṭhitaḥ || 373 ||
translation: It is only the dispassionate man who, being thoroughly grounded in Brahman, can give up the external attachment to the sense-objects and the internal attachment for egoism etc.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It is only the dispassionate man who, being thoroughly grounded in Brahman, can give up the external attachment to the sense-objects and the internal attachment for egoism etc.

sanskrit_shloka:
वैराग्यबोधौ पुरुषस्य पक्षिवत् पक्षौ विजानीहि विचक्षण त्वम् ।
विमुक्तिसौधाग्रलताधिरोहणं ताभ्यां विना नान्यतरेण सिध्यति ॥ ३७४ ॥
transliteration:
vairāgyabodhau puruṣasya pakṣivat pakṣau vijānīhi vicakṣaṇa tvam |
vimuktisaudhāgralatādhirohaṇaṃ tābhyāṃ vinā nānyatareṇa sidhyati || 374 ||
translation: Know, O wise man, dispassion and discrimination to be like the two wings of a bird in the case of an aspirant. Unless both are there, none can, with the help of either one, reach the creeper of Liberation that grows, as it were, on the top of an edifice.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Know, O wise man, dispassion and discrimination to be like the two wings of a bird in the case of an aspirant. Unless both are there, none can, with the help of either one, reach the creeper of Liberation that grows, as it were, on the top of an edifice.

sanskrit_shloka:
अत्यन्तवैराग्यवतः समाधिः समाहितस्यैव दृढप्रबोधः ।
प्रबुद्धतत्त्वस्य हि बन्धमुक्तिः मुक्तात्मनो नित्यसुखानुभूतिः ॥ ३७५ ॥
transliteration:
atyantavairāgyavataḥ samādhiḥ samāhitasyaiva dṛḍhaprabodhaḥ |
prabuddhatattvasya hi bandhamuktiḥ muktātmano nityasukhānubhūtiḥ || 375 ||
translation: The extremely dispassionate man alone has Samadhi, and the man of Samadhi alone gets steady realisation; the man who has realised the Truth is alone free from bondage, and the free soul only experiences eternal Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The extremely dispassionate man alone has Samadhi, and the man of Samadhi alone gets steady realisation; the man who has realised the Truth is alone free from bondage, and the free soul only experiences eternal Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
वैराग्यान्न परं सुखस्य जनकं पश्यामि वश्यात्मनः तच्चेच्छुद्धतरात्मबोधसहितं स्वाराज्यसाम्राज्यधुक् ।
एतद्द्वारमजस्रमुक्तियुवतेर्यस्मात्त्वमस्मात्परं सर्वत्रास्पृहया सदात्मनि सदा प्रज्ञां कुरु श्रेयसे ॥ ३७६ ॥
transliteration:
vairāgyānna paraṃ sukhasya janakaṃ paśyāmi vaśyātmanaḥ taccecchuddhatarātmabodhasahitaṃ svārājyasāmrājyadhuk |
etaddvāramajasramuktiyuvateryasmāttvamasmātparaṃ sarvatrāspṛhayā sadātmani sadā prajñāṃ kuru śreyase || 376 ||
translation: For the man of self-control I do not find any better instrument of happiness than dispassion, and if that is coupled with a highly pure realisation of the Self, it conduces to the suzerainty of absolute Independence; and since this is the gateway to the damsel of everlasting liberation, therefore for thy welfare, be dispassionate both internally and externally, and always fix thy mind on the eternal Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For the man of self-control I do not find any better instrument of happiness than dispassion, and if that is coupled with a highly pure realisation of the Self, it conduces to the suzerainty of absolute Independence; and since this is the gateway to the damsel of everlasting liberation, therefore for thy welfare, be dispassionate both internally and externally, and always fix thy mind on the eternal Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
आशां छिन्द्धि विषोपमेषु विषयेष्वेषैव मृत्योः कृतिस् त्यक्त्वा जातिकुलाश्रमेष्वभिमतिं मुञ्चातिदूरात्क्रियाः ।
देहादावसति त्यजात्मधिषणां प्रज्ञां कुरुष्वात्मनि त्वं द्रष्टास्यमनोऽसि निर्द्वयपरं ब्रह्मासि यद्वस्तुतः ॥ ३७७ ॥
transliteration:
āśāṃ chinddhi viṣopameṣu viṣayeṣveṣaiva mṛtyoḥ kṛtis tyaktvā jātikulāśrameṣvabhimatiṃ muñcātidūrātkriyāḥ |
dehādāvasati tyajātmadhiṣaṇāṃ prajñāṃ kuruṣvātmani tvaṃ draṣṭāsyamano'si nirdvayaparaṃ brahmāsi yadvastutaḥ || 377 ||
translation: Sever thy craving for the sense-objects, which are like poison, for it is the very image of death, and giving up thy pride of caste, family and order of life, fling actions to a distance. Give up thy identification with such unreal things as the body, and fix thy mind on the Ātman. For thou art really the Witness, Brahman, unshackled by the mind, the One without a second, and Supreme.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Sever thy craving for the sense-objects, which are like poison, for it is the very image of death, and giving up thy pride of caste, family and order of life, fling actions to a distance. Give up thy identification with such unreal things as the body, and fix thy mind on the Ātman. For thou art really the Witness, Brahman, unshackled by the mind, the One without a second, and Supreme.

sanskrit_shloka:
लक्ष्ये ब्रह्मणि मानसं दृढतरं संस्थाप्य बाह्येन्द्रियं स्वस्थाने विनिवेश्य निश्चलतनुश्चोपेक्ष्य देहस्थितिम् ।
ब्रह्मात्मैक्यमुपेत्य तन्मायातया चाखण्डवृत्त्यानिशं ब्रह्मानन्दरसं पिबात्मनि मुदा शून्यैः किमन्यैर्भृशम् ॥ ३७८ ॥
transliteration:
lakṣye brahmaṇi mānasaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ saṃsthāpya bāhyendriyaṃ svasthāne viniveśya niścalatanuścopekṣya dehasthitim |
brahmātmaikyamupetya tanMāyātayā cākhaṇḍavṛttyāniśaṃ brahmānandarasaṃ pibātmani mudā śūnyaiḥ kimanyairbhṛśam || 378 ||
translation: Fixing the mind firmly on the Ideal, Brahman, and restraining the external organs in their respective centres; with the body held steady and taking no thought for its maintenance; attaining identity with Brahman and being one with It – always drink joyfully of the Bliss of Brahman in thy own Self, without a break. What is the use of other things which are entirely hollow?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Fixing the mind firmly on the Ideal, Brahman, and restraining the external organs in their respective centres; with the body held steady and taking no thought for its maintenance; attaining identity with Brahman and being one with It – always drink joyfully of the Bliss of Brahman in thy own Self, without a break. What is the use of other things which are entirely hollow?

sanskrit_shloka:
अनात्मचिन्तनं त्यक्त्वा कश्मलं दुःखकारणम् ।
चिन्तयात्मानमानन्दरूपं यन्मुक्तिकारणम् ॥ ३७९ ॥
transliteration:
anātmacintanaṃ tyaktvā kaśmalaṃ duḥkhakāraṇam |
cintayātmānamānandarūpaṃ yanmuktikāraṇam || 379 ||
translation: Giving up the thought of the non-Self which is evil and productive of misery, think of the Self, the Bliss Absolute, which conduces to Liberation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Giving up the thought of the non-Self which is evil and productive of misery, think of the Self, the Bliss Absolute, which conduces to Liberation.

sanskrit_shloka:
एष स्वयंज्योतिरशेषसाक्षी विज्ञानकोशो विलसत्यजस्रम् ।
लक्ष्यं विधायैनमसद्विलक्षणम् अखण्डवृत्त्यात्मतयानुभावय ॥ ३८0 ॥
transliteration:
eṣa svayaṃjyotiraśeṣasākṣī vijñānakośo vilasatyajasram |
lakṣyaṃ vidhāyainamasadvilakṣaṇam akhaṇḍavṛttyātmatayānubhāvaya || 380 ||
translation: Here shines eternally the Ātman, the Self-effulgent Witness of everything, which has the Buddhi for Its seat. Making this Ātman which is distinct from the unreal, the goal, meditate on It as thy own Self, excluding all other thought.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Here shines eternally the Ātman, the Self-effulgent Witness of everything, which has the Buddhi for Its seat. Making this Ātman which is distinct from the unreal, the goal, meditate on It as thy own Self, excluding all other thought.

sanskrit_shloka:
एतमच्छीन्नया वृत्त्या प्रत्ययान्तरशून्यया ।
उल्लेखयन्विजानीयात्स्वस्वरूपतया स्फुटम् ॥ ३८१ ॥
transliteration:
etamacchīnnayā vṛttyā pratyayāntaraśūnyayā |
ullekhayanvijānīyātsvasvarūpatayā sphuṭam || 381 ||
translation: Reflecting on this Ātman continuously and without any foreign thought intervening, one must distinctly realise It to be one’s real Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Reflecting on this Ātman continuously and without any foreign thought intervening, one must distinctly realise It to be one’s real Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
अत्रात्मत्वं दृढीकुर्वन्नहमादिषु संत्यजन् ।
उदासीनतया तेषु तिष्ठेत्स्फुटघटादिवत् ॥ ३८२ ॥
transliteration:
atrātmatvaṃ dṛḍhīkurvannahamādiṣu saṃtyajan |
udāsīnatayā teṣu tiṣṭhetsphuṭaghaṭādivat || 382 ||
translation: Strengthening one’s identification with This, and giving up that with egoism and the rest, one must live without any concern for them, as if they were trifling things, like a cracked jar or the like.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Strengthening one’s identification with This, and giving up that with egoism and the rest, one must live without any concern for them, as if they were trifling things, like a cracked jar or the like.

sanskrit_shloka:
विशुद्धमन्तःकरणं स्वरूपे निवेश्य साक्षिण्यवबोधमात्रे ।
शनैः शनैर्निश्चलतामुपानयन् पूर्णं स्वमेवानुविलोकयेत्ततः ॥ ३८३ ॥
transliteration:
viśuddhamantaḥkaraṇaṃ svarūpe niveśya sākṣiṇyavabodhamātre |
śanaiḥ śanairniścalatāmupānayan pūrṇaṃ svamevānuvilokayettataḥ || 383 ||
translation: Fixing the purified mind in the Self, the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute, and slowly making it still, one must then realise one’s own infinite Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Fixing the purified mind in the Self, the Witness, the Knowledge Absolute, and slowly making it still, one must then realise one’s own infinite Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहेन्द्रियप्राणमनोऽहमादिभिः स्वाज्ञानकॢप्तैरखिलैरुपाधिभिः ।
विमुक्तमात्मानमखण्डरूपं पूर्णं महाकाशमिवावलोकयेत् ॥ ३८४ ॥
transliteration:
dehendriyaprāṇamano'hamādibhiḥ svājñānakḷptairakhilairupādhibhiḥ |
vimuktamātmānamakhaṇḍarūpaṃ pūrṇaṃ mahākāśamivāvalokayet || 384 ||
translation: One should behold the Ātman, the Indivisible and Infinite, free from all limiting adjuncts such as the body, organs, Prāṇas, Manas and egoism, which are creations of one’s own ignorance – like the infinite sky.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: One should behold the Ātman, the Indivisible and Infinite, free from all limiting adjuncts such as the body, organs, Prāṇas, Manas and egoism, which are creations of one’s own ignorance – like the infinite sky.

sanskrit_shloka:
घटकलशकुसूलसूचिमुख्यैः गगनमुपाधिशतैर्विमुक्तमेकम् ।
भवति न विविधं तथैव शुद्धं परमहमादिविमुक्तमेकमेव ॥ ३८५ ॥
transliteration:
ghaṭakalaśakusūlasūcimukhyaiḥ gaganamupādhiśatairvimuktamekam |
bhavati na vividhaṃ tathaiva śuddhaṃ paramahamādivimuktamekameva || 385 ||
translation: The sky, divested of the hundreds of limiting adjuncts such as a jar, a pitcher, a receptacle for grains or a needle, is one, and not diverse; exactly in a similar way the pure Brahman, when divested of egoism etc., is verily One.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sky, divested of the hundreds of limiting adjuncts such as a jar, a pitcher, a receptacle for grains or a needle, is one, and not diverse; exactly in a similar way the pure Brahman, when divested of egoism etc., is verily One.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्ता मृषामात्रा उपाधयः ।
ततः पूर्णं स्वमात्मानं पश्येदेकात्मना स्थितम् ॥ ३८६ ॥
transliteration:
brahmādistambaparyantā mṛṣāmātrā upādhayaḥ |
tataḥ pūrṇaṃ svamātmānaṃ paśyedekātmanā sthitam || 386 ||
translation: The limiting adjuncts from Brahma down to a clump of grass are all wholly unreal. Therefore one should realise one’s own Infinite Self as the only Principle.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The limiting adjuncts from Brahma down to a clump of grass are all wholly unreal. Therefore one should realise one’s own Infinite Self as the only Principle.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्र भ्रान्त्या कल्पितं तद्विवेके तत्तन्मात्रं नैव तस्माद्विभिन्नम् ।
भ्रान्तेर्नाशे भाति दृष्टाहितत्त्वं रज्जुस्तद्वद्विश्वमात्मस्वरूपम् ॥ ३८७ ॥
transliteration:
yatra bhrāntyā kalpitaṃ tadviveke tattanmātraṃ naiva tasmādvibhinnam |
bhrānternāśe bhāti dṛṣṭāhitattvaṃ rajjustadvadviśvamātmasvarūpam || 387 ||
translation: That in which something is imagined to exist through error, is, when rightly discriminated, that thing itself, and not distinct from it. When the error is gone, the reality about the snake falsely perceived becomes the rope. Similarly the universe is in reality the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That in which something is imagined to exist through error, is, when rightly discriminated, that thing itself, and not distinct from it. When the error is gone, the reality about the snake falsely perceived becomes the rope. Similarly the universe is in reality the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वयं ब्रह्मा स्वयं विष्णुः स्वयमिन्द्रः स्वयं शिवः ।
स्वयं विश्वमिदं सर्वं स्वस्मादन्यन्न किंचन ॥ ३८८ ॥
transliteration:
svayaṃ brahmā svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ svayamindraḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ |
svayaṃ viśvamidaṃ sarvaṃ svasmādanyanna kiṃcana || 388 ||
translation: The Self is Brahma, the Self is Vishnu, the Self is Indra, the Self is Shiva; the Self is all this universe. Nothing exists except the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Self is Brahma, the Self is Vishnu, the Self is Indra, the Self is Shiva; the Self is all this universe. Nothing exists except the Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
अन्तः स्वयं चापि बहिः स्वयं च स्वयं पुरस्तात्स्वयमेव पश्चात् ।
स्वयं ह्यावाच्यां स्वयमप्युदीच्यां तथोपरिष्टात्स्वयमप्यधस्तात् ॥ ३८९ ॥
transliteration:
antaḥ svayaṃ cāpi bahiḥ svayaṃ ca svayaṃ purastātsvayameva paścāt |
svayaṃ hyāvācyāṃ svayamapyudīcyāṃ tathopariṣṭātsvayamapyadhastāt || 389 ||
translation: The Self is within, and the Self is without; the Self is before and the Self is behind; the Self is in the south, and the Self is in the north; the Self likewise is above as also below.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Self is within, and the Self is without; the Self is before and the Self is behind; the Self is in the south, and the Self is in the north; the Self likewise is above as also below.

sanskrit_shloka:
तरङ्गफेनभ्रमबुद्बुदादि सर्वं स्वरूपेण जलं यथा तथा ।
चिदेव देहाद्यहमन्तमेतत् सर्वं चिदेवैकरसं विशुद्धम् ॥ ३९0 ॥
transliteration:
taraṅgaphenabhramabudbudādi sarvaṃ svarūpeṇa jalaṃ yathā tathā |
cideva dehādyahamantametat sarvaṃ cidevaikarasaṃ viśuddham || 390 ||
translation: As the wave, the foam, the whirlpool, the bubble, etc., are all in essence but water, similarly the Chit (Knowledge Absolute) is all this, from the body up to egoism. Everything is verily the Chit, homogeneous and pure.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As the wave, the foam, the whirlpool, the bubble, etc., are all in essence but water, similarly the Chit (Knowledge Absolute) is all this, from the body up to egoism. Everything is verily the Chit, homogeneous and pure.

sanskrit_shloka:
सदेवेदं सर्वं जगदवगतं वाङ्मनसयोः सतोऽन्यन्नास्त्येव प्रकृतिपरसीम्नि स्थितवतः ।
पृथक्किं मृत्स्नायाः कलशघटकुम्भाद्यवगतं वदत्येष भ्रान्तस्त्वमहमिति मायामदिरया ॥ ३९१ ॥
transliteration:
sadevedaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavagataṃ vāṅmanasayoḥ sato'nyannāstyeva prakṛtiparasīmni sthitavataḥ |
pṛthakkiṃ mṛtsnāyāḥ kalaśaghaṭakumbhādyavagataṃ vadatyeṣa bhrāntastvamahamiti māyāmadirayā || 391 ||
translation: All this universe known through speech and mind is nothing but Brahman; there is nothing besides Brahman, which exists beyond the utmost range of the Prakriti. Are the pitcher, jug, jar, etc., known to be distinct from the clay of which they are composed? It is the deluded man who talks of 'thou' and 'I', as an effect of the wine of Māyā.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: All this universe known through speech and mind is nothing but Brahman; there is nothing besides Brahman, which exists beyond the utmost range of the Prakriti. Are the pitcher, jug, jar, etc., known to be distinct from the clay of which they are composed? It is the deluded man who talks of 'thou' and 'I', as an effect of the wine of Māyā.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्रियासमभिहारेण यत्र नान्यदिति श्रुतिः ।
ब्रवीति द्वैतराहित्यं मिथ्याध्यासनिवृत्तये ॥ ३९२ ॥
transliteration:
kriyāsamabhihāreṇa yatra nānyaditi śrutiḥ |
bravīti dvaitarāhityaṃ mithyādhyāsanivṛttaye || 392 ||
translation: The Śruti, in the passage, 'Where one sees nothing else', etc., declares by an accumulation of verbs the absence of duality, in order to remove the false superimpositions.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Śruti, in the passage, 'Where one sees nothing else', etc., declares by an accumulation of verbs the absence of duality, in order to remove the false superimpositions.

sanskrit_shloka:
आकाशवन्निर्मलनिर्विकल्पं निःसीमनिःस्पन्दननिर्विकारम् ।
अन्तर्बहिःशून्यमनन्यमद्वयं स्वयं परं ब्रह्म किमस्ति बोध्यम् ॥ ३९३ ॥
transliteration:
ākāśavannirmalanirvikalpaṃ niḥsīmaniḥspandananirvikāram |
antarbahiḥśūnyamananyamadvayaṃ svayaṃ paraṃ brahma kimasti bodhyam || 393 ||
translation: The Supreme Brahman is, like the sky, pure, absolute, infinite, motionless and changeless, devoid of interior or exterior, the One Existence, without a second, and is one’s own Self. Is there any other object of knowledge?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Supreme Brahman is, like the sky, pure, absolute, infinite, motionless and changeless, devoid of interior or exterior, the One Existence, without a second, and is one’s own Self. Is there any other object of knowledge?

sanskrit_shloka:
वक्तव्यं किमु विद्यतेऽत्र बहुधा ब्रह्मैव जीवः स्वयं ब्रह्मैतज्जगदाततं नु सकलं ब्रह्माद्वितीयं श्रुतिः ।
ब्रह्मैवाहमिति प्रबुद्धमतयः संत्यक्तबाह्याः स्फुटं ब्रह्मीभूय वसन्ति सन्ततचिदानन्दात्मनैतद्ध्रुवम् ॥ ३९४ ॥
transliteration:
vaktavyaṃ kimu vidyate'tra bahudhā brahmaiva jīvaḥ svayaṃ brahmaitajjagadātataṃ nu sakalaṃ brahmādvitīyaṃ śrutiḥ |
brahmaivāhamiti prabuddhamatayaḥ saṃtyaktabāhyāḥ sphuṭaṃ brahmībhūya vasanti santatacidānandātmanaitaddhruvam || 394 ||
translation: What is the use of dilating on this subject? The Jīva is no other than Brahman; this whole extended universe is Brahman Itself; the Śruti inculcates the Brahman without a second; and it is an indubitable fact that people of enlightened minds who know their identity with Brahman and have given up their connection with the objective world, live palpably unifold with Brahman as Eternal Knowledge and Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: What is the use of dilating on this subject? The Jīva is no other than Brahman; this whole extended universe is Brahman Itself; the Śruti inculcates the Brahman without a second; and it is an indubitable fact that people of enlightened minds who know their identity with Brahman and have given up their connection with the objective world, live palpably unifold with Brahman as Eternal Knowledge and Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
जहि मलमायाकोशेऽहंधियोत्थापिताशां प्रसभमनिलकल्पे लिङ्गदेहेऽपि पश्चात् ।
निगमगदितकीर्तिं नित्यमानन्दमूर्तिं स्वयमिति परिचीय ब्रह्मरूपेण तिष्ठ ॥ ३९५ ॥
transliteration:
jahi malaMāyākośe'haṃdhiyotthāpitāśāṃ prasabhamanilakalpe liṅgadehe'pi paścāt |
nigamagaditakīrtiṃ nityamānandamūrtiṃ svayamiti paricīya brahmarūpeṇa tiṣṭha || 395 ||
translation: (First) destroy the hopes raised by egoism in this filthy gross body, then do the same forcibly with the air-like subtle body; and realising Brahman, the embodiment of eternal Bliss – whose glories the Scriptures proclaim – as thy own Self, live as Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: (First) destroy the hopes raised by egoism in this filthy gross body, then do the same forcibly with the air-like subtle body; and realising Brahman, the embodiment of eternal Bliss – whose glories the Scriptures proclaim – as thy own Self, live as Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
शवाकारं यावद्भजति मनुजस्तावदशुचिः परेभ्यः स्यात्क्लेशो जननमरणव्याधिनिलयः ।
यदात्मानं शुद्धं कलयति शिवाकारमचलम् तदा तेभ्यो मुक्तो भवति हि तदाह श्रुतिरपि ॥ ३९६ ॥
transliteration:
śavākāraṃ yāvadbhajati manujastāvadaśuciḥ parebhyaḥ syātkleśo jananamaraṇavyādhinilayaḥ |
yadātmānaṃ śuddhaṃ kalayati śivākāramacalam tadā tebhyo mukto bhavati hi tadāha śrutirapi || 396 ||
translation: So long as man has any regard for this corpse-like body, he is impure, and suffers from his enemies as also from birth, death and disease; but when he thinks of himself as pure, as the essence of good and immovable, he assuredly becomes free from them; the Śrutis also say this.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: So long as man has any regard for this corpse-like body, he is impure, and suffers from his enemies as also from birth, death and disease; but when he thinks of himself as pure, as the essence of good and immovable, he assuredly becomes free from them; the Śrutis also say this.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वात्मन्यारोपिताशेषाभासर्वस्तुनिरासतः ।
स्वयमेव परं ब्रह्म पूर्णमद्वयमक्रियम् ॥ ३९७ ॥
transliteration:
svātmanyāropitāśeṣābhāsarvastunirāsataḥ |
svayameva paraṃ brahma pūrṇamadvayamakriyam || 397 ||
translation: By the elimination of all apparent existences superimposed on the soul, the supreme Brahman, Infinite, the One without a second and beyond action, remains as Itself.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: By the elimination of all apparent existences superimposed on the soul, the supreme Brahman, Infinite, the One without a second and beyond action, remains as Itself.

sanskrit_shloka:
समाहितायां सति चित्तवृत्तौ परात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे ।
न दृश्यते कश्चिदयं विकल्पः प्रजल्पमात्रः परिशिष्यते यतः ॥ ३९८ ॥
transliteration:
samāhitāyāṃ sati cittavṛttau parātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe |
na dṛśyate kaścidayaṃ vikalpaḥ prajalpamātraḥ pariśiṣyate yataḥ || 398 ||
translation: When the mind-functions are merged in the Paramātman, the Brahman, the Absolute, none of this phenomenal world is seen, whence it is reduced to mere talk.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the mind-functions are merged in the Paramātman, the Brahman, the Absolute, none of this phenomenal world is seen, whence it is reduced to mere talk.

sanskrit_shloka:
असत्कल्पो विकल्पोऽयं विश्वमित्येकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ३९९ ॥
transliteration:
asatkalpo vikalpo'yaṃ viśvamityekavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 399 ||
translation: In the One Entity (Brahman) the conception of the universe is a mere phantom. Whence can there be any diversity in That which is changeless, formless and Absolute?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the One Entity (Brahman) the conception of the universe is a mere phantom. Whence can there be any diversity in That which is changeless, formless and Absolute?

sanskrit_shloka:
द्रष्टुदर्शनदृश्यादिभावशून्यैकवस्तुनि ।
निर्विकारे निराकारे निर्विशेषे भिदा कुतः ॥ ४00 ॥
transliteration:
draṣṭudarśanadṛśyādibhāvaśūnyaikavastuni |
nirvikāre nirākāre nirviśeṣe bhidā kutaḥ || 400 ||
translation: In the One Entity devoid of the concepts of seer, seeing and seen – which is changeless, formless and Absolute – whence can there be any diversity?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the One Entity devoid of the concepts of seer, seeing and seen – which is changeless, formless and Absolute – whence can there be any diversity?
